title: Being offered In the Mood at a Lincoln Hotel rehearsal
summary: At a 2 a.m. rehearsal in the Blue Room of the Lincoln, a stranger offered an arrangement for his name; Barnet stopped it after 16 bars and sent the man to Glenn Miller: In the Mood.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose

Reel 3

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 347-5395
P R O C E E D I N G S
You were about to tell me an experience you had, on the end of the last reel.

Well, yes. First of all, I wanted to say that at all times, when you had a band and you were broadcasting or recording, there were always people bringing tunes to you and saying, 'Look, I'll put your name on it. You can publish it. You can put it in your company. If you'll just play it.' Now, this has not only happened to me, it's happened to everybody else that ever had a band. But I wanted to tell you about one particular event. We were having this rehearsal at the Blue Room, the Lincoln, at 2:00 o'clock in the morning, after hours, and this fellow came in, he said, 'I've got an arrangement here I'd like to have you try.' And he says, 'If you like it,' he says, 'you can put your name on it and you can publish it.' And I said, 'Well, I've got to do what we've got to do first. If we have time, I'll be happy to run it over.' So we finally got done with what we were doing, and I said, 'Okay, pass it out.' And the band started and we played about 16 bars of it, and I stopped the band, and I said, 'I don't like it. I can't use it. Why don't you take it down to Glenn Miller,' and he did. That was 'In the Mood.'
So you're looking at a real smart guy,
picking tunes. I still don't like it.
